title: Quantifier elimination: equality patterns and dense orders
summary: Remove quantifiers from equality and dense-order formulas, then describe their definable sets and elementary inclusions.
abstract: For two rational numbers, a third lies above the first and below the second exactly when the first is smaller than the second. This replaces a statement about an unknown object by a comparison of the given objects. Quantifier elimination asks whether every formula can be simplified in this way, using the axioms of a particular theory. We carry out the simplification for infinite sets with equality alone and for dense linear orders without endpoints. In an infinite set, a definable subset is finite or has finite complement; in a dense order, it is a finite union of intervals and points, with endpoints among the parameters. The same arguments show that all models of each theory agree on sentences, and that inclusions between its models preserve every first-order statement about their elements.
